Optimum Nutrition vs Orgain protein powder

Start with dairy versus plant protein. Then compare equal amounts of protein, rather than scoop count.

By FitGear Authority editorial · Label sources checked November 1, 2026

As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases. This is a comparison of manufacturer information, not a hands-on taste or performance test. Check the exact flavor and size before ordering.

Which one fits your shopping needs?

If you want to compare a whey powder and do not exclude dairy, start with the Gold Standard label. If you want a plant-based powder, start with Orgain. This is a choice of format, not a claim that one is universally better. Neither should be chosen solely because its tub has more scoops or a familiar brand name.

Gold Standard 100% Whey: what to check

The manufacturer lists 24 g protein per serving and identifies whey isolate as the primary protein source. That description does not mean the product is an isolate-only powder. Read the complete ingredient and allergen panels for the flavor you intend to buy.

Find Gold Standard Whey on Amazon (paid link) ↗

Orgain Organic Plant Based Protein: what to check

Orgain lists 21 g plant-based protein per serving. Its current Creamy Chocolate Fudge page describes a vegan formula. Confirm the exact product line: similarly named Orgain powders can have different ingredients. A plant-based label also does not replace checking your specific allergens.

Find Orgain Plant Protein on Amazon (paid link) ↗

Compare value fairly

A scoop is a manufacturer-defined measure. Comparing the price of one scoop from each tub can be misleading when protein quantities differ. Instead, record the delivered price, servings per package, and protein grams per serving for each exact listing. Use our protein value calculator to compare cost for 25 g protein.

For an arithmetic example, a hypothetical $40 package with 30 servings and 24 g protein per serving costs about $1.39 per 25 g protein. That is a calculation example, not a current product price or a recommended serving. Include shipping and read subscription terms before comparing the total.

When to skip either purchase

Skip a large tub when you have not decided which flavor or format you will use. Skip a subscription if you only want a trial purchase. If the ingredient or allergen label is unclear, ask the manufacturer before ordering. This comparison cannot determine personal medical suitability.

Questions before checkout

Does 24 g versus 21 g make one automatically better?

No. The listed grams help compare quantities, but your ingredient preferences, full label, package cost, and intended use also matter.

Have you tested taste or mixing?

No. We have not tested these products. Manufacturer facts and our shopping interpretation are kept separate.

Are these links to an exact Amazon listing?

They open product-name searches. Match the exact formula, flavor, size, seller, and current label before purchasing.
